f1-01.text: The Fairlinks Golf Network runs the screens at 100 connected golf clubs, from one Personalisation Hub account.
Every club has the same six screen types.
Whatever the network sets up once goes live at every club.

f1-02.text: The network has six screen types: the pro shop, the driving range, the first tee, the halfway house, the locker room and the clubhouse bar.
They're set once, and every club on the network has them.

f1-03.text: Each one has its own playlist.
First, the pro shop playlist is set to rotate three campaigns, one after another.
New slots belong to Headquarters, for the network's own promotions.
Slot one is the one the network will sell to brands.
Its owner changes from Headquarters to Advertiser.
One slot in three now earns media revenue, and two keep promoting the network's own offers.

f1-04.text: The driving range, first tee, halfway house, locker room and clubhouse bar get the same setup, in a few clicks.
The network decides exactly how much screen time it sells.
Set once, live at all 100 clubs: the same six brand partner slots now exist at every club.
f1-04.cue: Set once, live at all 100 clubs

f1-05.text: Corvane Golf is already set up as a direct advertiser, next to the advertisers synced from DSPs.

f1-06.text: Slots are always sold through deals. A brand is never assigned to a slot directly.
This direct deal gives Corvane all of December across the whole network at a fixed CPM, and it's never sent to a DSP.

f1-07.text: The six new brand partner slots start unassigned, so nothing plays in them yet.
Corvane's deal is saved as a draft, ready to place on the slots.
f1-07.cue: The new deal, not on a slot yet

f1-07.text: Each slot's list offers DSPs for open auction, and deals.
The network picks the Corvane deal for all six.
Direct deals and programmatic demand are managed side by side, in one place.
All six slots now carry the deal, at every one of the 100 clubs. Then, save the changes.

f1-08.text: The forecast plays cover all 100 clubs, for reference only: this is a direct buy at a fixed CPM.
Finalising puts the deal live, and its revenue is reported just like DSP revenue.
Every December window on all six screen types, at all 100 clubs, is now Corvane's.
f1-08.cue: Live · direct, not sent to a DSP

f1-09.text: Finally, the network invites Corvane with its own Advertiser login, so the brand can manage its own campaigns.
Jamie gets the Advertiser role, so Jamie only ever sees Corvane's campaigns.
The invitation goes out, and the network's first brand partner deal is done.

f2-01.text: Jamie from Corvane signs in with the login the network provided. Corvane can run its own campaigns, or leave them to the network.
Everything Jamie sees is scoped to Corvane's own campaigns.

f2-02.text: To start a new campaign, Jamie selects Launch a New Campaign, at the top of the list.

f2-03.text: There's no form to fill in. Jamie just talks, and the AI campaign agent listens.
As Jamie speaks, it captures the campaign name, products, objective, screens and audience.
A whole campaign brief, in the time it takes to describe it.

f2-04.text: The agent writes the brief from what Jamie said, and from how past campaigns performed.
It's ready in seconds, with nothing typed by hand.
Corvane's deal ID is pre-selected, so the campaign can only use the slots on that deal.
Name, details, products, audience and objective are all filled in.
Only the deal's six screen types are switched on.

f2-05.text: Next, the agent writes the headline and copy from the agreed brand guidelines: Corvane's, the network's, or an agreed mix of both.
Every word can be edited before any creative is made.

f2-06.text: With the copy agreed, the agent generates a creative preview of the first and last frames.
The frames follow the agreed brand guidelines, and draw on what worked best in past campaigns.
Not quite right? Jamie asks for a change in plain English, like a greener background for the driving range.
And the frame is regenerated with the change.

f2-07.text: Generate Creative Assets builds the final creative for every screen type, from the pro shop to the clubhouse bar.
Once the approved campaign runs, its results feed Corvane's future campaigns, closing the loop.

f2-08.text: Corvane also wants a second campaign, just for low-handicap members, at every club on the network.
Targeting is set on the campaign's Targeting tab, exactly as the network would.
Jamie adds a rule: Audience Segments includes Low-handicap members.
Every option is a drop-down, so there's nothing to type and nothing to get wrong.
Only the data sources, attributes and values the network has approved for brands appear here.
The network controls 100% of the targeting it shares.
The data stays in the network's own cloud. Corvane only ever picks a segment.

f2-09.text: A second rule adds purchase history from the pro shops' point-of-sale data, across the network.
Purchase History includes golf balls, again picked from a list.
Targeting on real membership and sales data is what makes the network so valuable to brands.
Low-handicap members who buy golf balls match both rules, and Jamie saves the targeting with Save Changes.
Saving doesn't submit anything. Send for approval, at the top right, sends the campaign to Fairlinks.
It's now awaiting approval, with no activation toggle until Fairlinks approves it.

f2-10.text: Every brand campaign needs Fairlinks' approval before it can play on the network. Corvane's is waiting in Campaign Approval.
One click on Approve Selected, and Corvane's members campaign is approved, with its own creative ID.
Once it's approved, the activation toggle appears in place of Send for approval.

f3-01.text: Now one club on the network: Fernhollow Golf Club. Hannah, a low-handicap member, arrives for her morning tee time.
Fernhollow's app welcomes her by name and invites her to check in.
One tap, and she's checked in for her round.
Corvane's members offer is first in her app.
f3-01.cue: Corvane's offer, in the club's app

f3-02.text: Her check-in links to what the club already knows: her membership and what she buys in the pro shop.
She matches both of Corvane's rules, in real time.

f3-03.text: Every screen rotates three campaigns: two of the network's own, and the brand partner slot it sells.
Most golfers see Corvane's standard creative in that slot.
Checked in at the pro shop, she sees Corvane's members version, personalised for her.
On the driving range, it shows the new driver as she warms up.
At the first tee, the same campaign follows her to the start of her round.
At the halfway house, it reminds her of the free sleeve of Tour balls.
In the locker room, it invites her to book a driver fitting.
And at the clubhouse bar, it's waiting for her after the round.
Back at the pro shop, the fitting is booked and her free sleeve is applied. One member, six screens, one offer sold by the network.

f3-04.text: Now back to the whole network. Corvane holds slot one on all six screen types at all 100 clubs, every day of December.
Each booking carries the default creative and the personalised members version, both approved.

f3-05.text: Booking revenue is for the whole network: 100 clubs, six screen types, every window sold at Corvane's fixed CPM.
That's over three and a half million dollars in two weeks, from one slot in three.
